title: RoutingTable
description: Normative shape of the routing table for agent/contracts/role-routing@1.0.0 - one table per account, created when the first profile is saved, edited only through settings, and validated against this file before it is saved. Revised from 0.1.0: the six closed role names become routing TIERS named by entries in agent/contracts/role-registry@1.0.0, so the map is keyed by tier name rather than by a fixed six-member record. Two properties the closed record used to guarantee structurally are kept: the six built-in tiers are still required to be present, because the six built-in role entries cannot be removed and a tier that is absent is how one quietly acquires an implicit default (INV-AG-24); and the table still admits no member beyond the two it declares, because a table-wide fallback profile is the substitution rule arriving by the back door, which INV-AG-23 forbids. What this file cannot know is which further tiers the account's registry names - that reconciliation is stated in the contract document and reports an absent tier as unassigned, never as a default. The split the defaults propose is the measured one - VERIFIED (spikes/SP-17-provider-matrix/REPORT.md#1-tra-loi-tung-cau-hoi Q1, Q3, Q6).

tableVersion.description: The version of the role-routing contract this table was written against. The table replicates between devices on different builds: a newer build reads an older table unchanged, and an older build meeting a newer version refuses the whole table (TABLE_VERSION_AHEAD), because reading around an unrecognised member here would mean running a tier on a model the user assigned to something else.

assignments.description: One assignment per routing tier, keyed by tier name. The six built-in tiers are required because the six built-in role entries that name them cannot be removed; any further key is a tier contributed by an account-authored or pack-contributed role entry. An unassigned tier is represented by the explicit unassigned state and never by the key being absent - absence is reported against the registry, never resolved to a default.

TierName.description: The name of a routing tier: the slot a model is assigned to. Open where the 0.1.0 role union was closed, but not free-form - a tier name is lower-case kebab-case so that the name a role entry writes and the key this table holds cannot differ by case or spacing. A key matching this pattern that no registry entry names is reported as TIER_UNKNOWN and is never resolved.

Assignment.description: What a tier points at, or the explicit statement that it points at nothing. An assignment carries no capability list of its own: what a model offers belongs to agent/contracts/provider-profile@0.1.0 and what a tier requires belongs to the role entries naming it in agent/contracts/role-registry@1.0.0. A second copy here would be the one that goes stale when the user edits the profile - stale in the direction that sends an image to a model that can no longer read one.

acknowledgedUnmeasured.description: True when the user confirmed an assignment the product holds no measurement for. The product does not enforce a judgement it has no way to make; it states what was measured and records that the user decided anyway.
